title: Case: A delivered household item is confirmed broken
context: The merchant has already reviewed its inline damage-inspection record. The next action is a replacement request to the party authorised to approve it.
initial_request: I would prefer the same lamp rather than a refund. Please ask the merchant to approve a replacement.

events.body: Inline inspection record TG-7079: ceramic table lamp arrived with a separated base; recipient report reviewed against our returned-item inspection. Damage accepted for replacement assessment. Dispatch DL-7796 has completed; replacement approval is not yet recorded.
I would prefer the same lamp rather than a refund. Please ask the merchant to approve a replacement.
I would prefer the same lamp rather than a refund. Please ask the merchant to approve a replacement.

acceptable_actions.summary: Request replacement authorisation from the merchant using the accepted damage evidence.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Any team at Pebblewick Goods that appears in the history
acceptable_actions.summary: Request replacement authorisation from the merchant using the accepted damage evidence. (asking that team to act or to route it to the team that owns it)

must_not: Merchant approval and reserved stock do not establish replacement dispatch or receipt.
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: Please approve a like-for-like lamp replacement for TG-7079 using your accepted inspection record. Isolde has selected replacement in the order thread.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-022: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
